name: Salmon Color
lede: Salmon Color is a soft yellowish pink named after the fish; in the books it appears as the pale untreated look of morganite, a pink beryl.

sections.title: A fish's pink
sections.body: Ridgway listed Salmon Color in 1886 and on plate XIV of 1912, and the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 calls it a moderate yellowish pink [2]. The name is a longer form of [[salmon]], and its neighbors include [[salmon-pink]], [[peach]] and [[coral]] [2].

sections.title: Morganite
sections.body: Finlay writes that a new pink beryl found on Madagascar in 1911 was named morganite as thanks to Morgan, a great collector of gems [1]. Freshly mined, it tends to be a pale, plain salmon, and heating can make it look vivid [1]. So the pale color is how the stone arrives, and heat is what changes it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive it appears in 0.39% of paintings (93), more common than half the named colors, as photographed [3]. It is most often a light inside the painting, and peaks in the 1900s [3]. The earliest match is a painting of 1420 [3].
